knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Slurry can run into drains and dry into airborne dust, and an unmarked wet floor is a slip hazard.
Dry sweeping and compressed air are not permitted. Slurry is collected by a rated method or kept in contained collection.
Marking the wet area warns people and manages the slip risk.
Stopping the water and containing the flow limits the release. The event is reported and recorded under the site procedure.

practicalCriteria: Sets up containment and drain protection before the first pass
Cleans slurry as the work proceeds, using approved methods
Marks and manages the wet area
Responds correctly when slurry reaches a drain
passRule: Knowledge checks: 4 of 5 correct (80%). Practical sign-off is separate and is not granted by the knowledge check: an assessor must observe every critical practical criterion and record it.
evidenceRequired: Slurry disposal record and incident record where applicable
stopWorkCriteria: Slurry reaches a drain and cannot be contained at once
Floor cannot be made safe for workers or the public
